articles.title: NASA Invites Media, Public to Join Voyager 1 One-Light Day Activities
articles.description: Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. NASA will highlight […]
articles.summary: NASA celebrates Voyager 1's historic milestone as it reaches one light-day distance from Earth after nearly 50 years of exploration. This remarkable achievement invites the public to celebrate humanity's most distant robotic explorer.

articles.title: First Direct Measurement of Cosmic Hydrogen Could Change How We Map the Universe
articles.description: The MeerKLASS international collaboration achieves the first direct measurement of the large-scale clustering of cosmic hydrogen in the Universe.
articles.summary: The MeerKLASS collaboration achieves the first direct measurement of large-scale cosmic hydrogen clustering, opening new ways to map the universe's structure and composition.

articles.title: Euclid offers best-ever 3D map of the universe to date
articles.description: The Euclid Consortium and the European Space Agency (ESA) have released the first major batch of data from the Euclid space telescope. This release, which captures light from more than a billion objects and covers an area of sky equivalent to 9,500 full moons, lays the foundation for Europe's dark universe detective's largest-ever 3D map of the cosmos. Several German research facilities play crucial roles in the Euclid mission's success.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The ESA's Euclid spacecraft releases its first major data batch, creating the most detailed 3D map of the universe ever produced to study dark matter and cosmic expansion.

articles.title: Europe's Hera spacecraft begins close inspections of an asteroid rammed by NASA in a 2022 test
articles.description: A European spacecraft has begun close inspections of an asteroid rammed by NASA four years ago in a planetary defense test.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Europe's Hera spacecraft begins detailed inspections of an asteroid struck by NASA's DART mission in 2022, validating planetary defense capabilities for protecting Earth.

articles.title: Independent technique validates landmark M87* image
articles.description: The 2019 Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) image was the work of hundreds of scientists and captured the first direct view of a black hole's shadow—becoming one of the most recognized scientific images of the modern era. A team of four from CSIRO, Australia's national science agency, has developed a powerful new imaging technique that validated the landmark 2019 image of the black hole at the center of galaxy M87.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: An independent technique validates the landmark 2019 Event Horizon Telescope image of M87*, confirming the first direct visual evidence of a black hole and its shadow.

articles.title: A massive new simulation reveals how the universe emerged from darkness
articles.description: A groundbreaking new supercomputer simulation is revealing how the universe escaped its cosmic dark age and transformed into a cosmos filled with stars and galaxies. Called Lumina, it recreates 2 billion years of early cosmic history across a region 1.6 billion light-years wide, capturing extraordinary details that previous simulations could not.
articles.summary: A groundbreaking supercomputer simulation reveals how the universe emerged from its cosmic dark age and transformed into the light-filled cosmos we observe today.

articles.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
articles.description: NASA has revealed an accelerated plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with SpaceX and Blue Origin developing competing lunar landers and a crucial orbital test scheduled for 2027. Faster rocket preparations, new lightweight spacesuits, and redesigned missions could help pave the way for a permanent lunar presence and future human exploration of Mars.
articles.summary: NASA announces an accelerated plan to return astronauts to the Moon by 2028, with SpaceX and Blue Origin developing landing systems for this landmark mission.

articles.title: Caltech robot makes history by building a structure in space
articles.description: For the first time, a robot has autonomously built part of a structure in space, demonstrating a breakthrough that could fundamentally change space exploration. The technology could one day allow scientists to construct enormous telescopes, communications antennas, and solar power stations in orbit, far beyond the size limits of today's rockets.
articles.summary: A Caltech robot has autonomously constructed part of a structure in space for the first time, opening new possibilities for space-based manufacturing and construction.

articles.title: Dark matter breakthrough coming? Euclid space telescope unveils its 1st look into the dark universe (video)
articles.description: The Euclid space telescope released its first major batch of data, capturing the light of more than a billion objects over an area of sky as big as 9,500 full moons.
articles.summary: The Euclid space telescope has released its first major data batch, capturing light from over a billion objects to advance our understanding of dark matter and the universe's structure.

articles.title: Astronomers stunned after James Webb Space Telescope discovers the earliest pair of black hole-powered quasars
articles.description: Using the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers have discovered the oldest pair of black hole-powered quasars ever seen. There's just one problem: they shouldn't exist!
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has discovered the oldest pair of black hole-powered quasars ever observed, pushing back the timeline of supermassive black hole formation.

articles.title: SpaceX Starship Flight 15 live updates: Super Heavy rocket moved to launch pad for 1st Starship double landing test
articles.description: SpaceX is counting down to make history with the launch of its Starship Flight 15 mission on Friday, Nov. 13, with liftoff scheduled for 5:45 p.m. EDT (2245 GMT) at Starbase, Texas. Starship Flight 15 will attempt to land both Starship Ship and Super Heavy Bo…
articles.summary: SpaceX is preparing for Starship Flight 15 on November 13, aiming to achieve the historic first synchronized double landing of Super Heavy booster rockets, marking a major milestone in reusable rocket technology.

articles.title: NASA’s Hubble Offers Cosmic Sampler of Targets for Roman
articles.description: A gallery of gravitational lenses captured by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope showcases the diversity of this cosmic phenomenon and lays the groundwork for follow-up observations by the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope has captured a stunning gallery of gravitational lenses that will serve as targets for the upcoming Roman Space Telescope. This collection showcases the remarkable diversity of gravitational lensing phenomena across the cosmos.

articles.title: APOD: 2026 November 11 – NGC 4449: Small Galaxy, Big Impact
articles.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 11 – NGC… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss   APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. NGC 4449: […]
articles.summary: The small galaxy NGC 4449 demonstrates surprisingly powerful gravitational influence on its surroundings despite its diminutive size. This discovery challenges conventional understanding of galactic dynamics and interaction.

articles.title: Astrophysicists Want to Forecast When a Black Hole Launches Its Jets
articles.description: Astrophysical jets are enormously powerful and energetic phenomena. Black holes launch them from their poles and they can extend enormous distances into space, disrupting star formation in adjacent regions. Astrophysicists want to be able to forecast when they're launched so they can understand theire extreme physics better. New research is making progress in understanding when they are triggered.
articles.summary: Astrophysicists are developing methods to forecast when black holes launch their powerful relativistic jets from their poles. This research advances understanding of some of the universe's most energetic phenomena.

articles.title: The Ice Giants' Magnetic Fields are Very Strange Compared to Earth's
articles.description: Uranus and Neptune, the Solar System's ice giants, have interiors unlike the other planets. As a result, they also have magnetic fields unlike the others. They're messy and tilted, and Voyager 2, the only spacecraft to even flyby them, showed us how messy they are. New research uses models to try to understand what's going on with the pair of planets and their weird fields, and found that it's likely they change on very short timescales. They could already be much different than when Voyager 2 visited in the late 1980s.
articles.summary: Uranus and Neptune possess remarkably unusual magnetic fields that differ dramatically from Earth's, reflecting their unique internal structures as ice giants. This discovery reveals fascinating diversity in planetary magnetism.

articles.title: The Chandra X-Ray Observatory Unmasks a Supernova Impostor
articles.description: Some stars, called Luminous Blue Variables, can be confused with supernovae explosions. They exhibit similar outbursts, but unlike supernovae, which explode once and then are gone forever, these stars have periodic outbursts. New research found that one of these 'supernova impostors' is in a binary relationship with a black hole or a neutron star, and that explains its periodic outbursts.
articles.summary: The Chandra X-Ray Observatory distinguishes between Luminous Blue Variables and actual supernovae explosions, revealing previously hidden stellar phenomena. This capability enhances our understanding of stellar evolution and explosive events.

articles.title: Planets Don't Just Disappear, But They Can Wobble Out of Sight if Their Neighbour is Close Enough
articles.description: TESS watched an exoplanet about 1,000 light years away as it repeatedly transited in front of its star for seven years. But astronomers were surprised to find that the hot Jupiter disappeared. Of course, planets don't just disappear. Something interrupted its transits from our point of view, and astronomers think they've figured out what happened. An unseen, nearby giant planet companion tugged on it until TESS couldn't see it anymore.
articles.summary: TESS observations reveal that exoplanets can experience orbital wobbling from neighboring planets that periodically obscures their transits from our view. This discovery demonstrates the complex gravitational dynamics of distant planetary systems.

articles.title: Automated Assembly in Space is the Future and NOM4D is Showing the Way
articles.description: The ability to build large structures in space is maturing. The ISS, Mir, and Tiangong were built in space from pre-constructed modules, but a new program called NOM4D is taking space construction to the next level. It recently showed that a simple robot can create truss-like structures in space from premade components. Is the sky the limit for NOM4D?
articles.summary: Automated assembly technology is maturing rapidly, enabling the construction of large structures in space as demonstrated by the ISS, Mir, and Tiangong stations. NOM4D exemplifies the future of in-situ manufacturing and space infrastructure development.

articles.title: ALMA Reveals a Jet of Cool Gas from a Microquasar
articles.description: There's a strange gamma-ray emitter in the Large Magellanic Cloud that has astronomers stumped about its source. It lies within the ashes left behind by a supernova that created a compact object that's part of the system. The supernova remnant provides some evidence for the emissions, but not the whole story.
articles.summary: ALMA's observations reveal a jet of cool gas emanating from a mysterious microquasar in the Large Magellanic Cloud. This discovery sheds new light on the nature of enigmatic gamma-ray emitters and relativistic jet formation.

articles.title: A new view of the gamma-ray gap: 14 years of Fermi data reveal around 450 sources in a largely unexplored energy range
articles.description: The universe is filled with light at many different energies. Some of it is invisible to our eyes, including extremely energetic gamma rays, which can only be produced in the most extreme environments in our universe, for example supermassive black holes, exploding stars or astrophysical jets. To "see" gamma rays, astrophysicists use particle experiments in space, such as the Fermi-Large Area Telescope (Fermi-LAT). This instrument was launched into space by NASA in 2008, and it can detect photons from 20 megaelectronvolts (MeV, a unit of energy) to beyond 1 teraelectronvolt (TeV).
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Fermi telescope data reveals approximately 450 gamma-ray sources in a previously unexplored energy range, expanding our understanding of high-energy phenomena across the cosmos.

articles.title: Simulated collisions reveal how Phobos could preserve rocks blasted off Mars
articles.description: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, but their origins remain uncertain. Were they asteroids captured by Mars' gravity, or did they form from debris following a giant impact on the planet?
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Collision simulations show how Mars's moon Phobos could preserve rocks ejected from the Martian surface, providing insights into the origins of Mars's enigmatic moons.

articles.title: Centaurus A in the spotlight: Plasma simulations reproduce black hole jets' mysterious bright edges
articles.description: Around 12 million light-years away, the supermassive black hole of the galaxy Centaurus A is hurling two enormous plasma jets into space at nearly the speed of light. These so-called jets are brighter at their edges than at their center. The reason for this was previously unclear but has now been explained by a team from the Chair of Astronomy at the University of Würzburg. The research is published in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Plasma simulations explain the mysterious bright edges of jets ejected by the supermassive black hole in Centaurus A, located 12 million light-years away.

articles.title: Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water
articles.description: Earth's water may have been born in the planet's fiery atmosphere rather than delivered by icy comets or asteroids. Scientists discovered that rocky pebbles reacting with hydrogen under extreme heat can produce water in minutes, potentially generating hundreds of oceans' worth during Earth's formation. The findings suggest that water may be a natural part of how rocky planets form, rather than something that must arrive from space.
articles.summary: New research suggests Earth's water may have originated in our planet's early atmosphere rather than being delivered by comets or asteroids, rewriting water's origin story.

articles.title: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe discovers a hidden pattern in the Sun’s chaotic magnetic fields
articles.description: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe has revealed a surprising secret hidden within the chaos of space: turbulent magnetic fields reverse their direction of rotation when examined at extremely small scales. The discovery exposes an unexpected pattern in solar wind turbulence that could help scientists better understand solar activity and predict geomagnetic storms.
articles.summary: NASA's Parker Solar Probe discovers hidden patterns in the Sun's turbulent magnetic fields, advancing our understanding of solar dynamics and space weather.

articles.title: NASA’s CHAPEA Mars crew finally emerges after more than a year in isolation
articles.description: After more than a year of simulated life on Mars, four NASA volunteers have finally emerged from isolation, bringing a remarkable space exploration experiment to an end. Their experiences growing food, conserving resources, and overcoming Mars-like challenges could help NASA prepare for humanity's future on the Moon and Mars.
articles.summary: Four NASA volunteers complete over a year of simulated Martian living in the CHAPEA habitat, providing valuable data for future human Mars exploration missions.

articles.title: A radical theory says the universe is twice as old as we thought
articles.description: A provocative new cosmological model suggests the Universe could be 26.7 billion years old and might not need dark matter or dark energy to explain its behavior. University of Ottawa researchers tested the theory against several major astronomical observations, finding that it could explain galaxy rotation, cosmic expansion, and the formation of early elements.
articles.summary: A new cosmological model proposes the universe could be 26.7 billion years old, challenging existing age estimates and potentially reshaping our understanding of cosmic history.

articles.title: The 'eclipse of the century' will plunge these 8 wonders of the Roman Empire into darkness on Aug. 2, 2027
articles.description: Ancient Roman cities, temples and amphitheaters across the Mediterranean will fall into the moon's shadow during the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027.
articles.summary: A total solar eclipse on August 2, 2027 will sweep across the Mediterranean, casting ancient Roman wonders into spectacular darkness for eclipse enthusiasts.

articles.title: NASA opens applications for astronauts who will live on the Moon
articles.description: If you ever wanted to earn a solid wage by living and working on another world, now's your chance. NASA has put out a call for a new generation of ast...
articles.summary: NASA has opened applications for astronauts who will live and work on the Moon, marking an exciting step toward sustained lunar exploration.

articles.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
articles.description: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning mor…
articles.summary: Physicists have discovered evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay occurring roughly once per 10 billion events, marking a significant breakthrough in fundamental physics after 42 years of research.

articles.title: Step inside the zeptoverse: British scientists use the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside a minuscule world where exotic particles may be hiding
articles.description: British scientists have used the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside the minuscule world of the zeptoverse.
articles.summary: British scientists at the Large Hadron Collider have peered into the zeptoverse, exploring the minuscule realm where exotic particles may exist and deepening our understanding of physics at the smallest scales.
